thread:
devon_support: Heads up — multiple customers reporting p95/p99 regressions on /v1/generate since ~10:05 UTC. Customer support cases 8421/8423 attached. Latency dashboard shows p95 up from ~120ms to ~720ms, p99 to ~1.8s. Error rates are normal.

maria_sre: thanks — any recent deploys or config changes in prod?

aj_runtime: there was a small rollout of runtime v2.14.1 at 09:58 (deploy #deploy-2026-03-15-0958). It was flagged as low-risk — only batching kernel tweaks + cache key normalization change.

ops-bot: Deploy deploy-2026-03-15-0958 to prod completed at 09:58:47 UTC :white_check_mark:

maria_sre: ok mark it as suspect. devon, do you have sample request_ids/trace ids?

devon_support: yep — sample request IDs: req_01FZVJ8Q, req_01FZVJ9B, req_01FZVKB0. Customers also provided traces: https://grafana.company.com/d/rt/latency?var-request=req_01FZVJ8Q

li_runtime: pulling traces now. Initial glance: tail latencies look like cache misses — KV cache miss rate spiked at deploy time. Prefetch hit rate dropped from 87% -> 24% for a subset of nodes.

maria_sre: metrics: can you paste the KV cache miss_rate and eviction_rate for the last hour?

li_runtime: paste from prometheus:
```
sum(increase(kv_cache_misses_total[5m])) by (pool) = 1860
sum(increase(kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) by (pool) = 520
kv_evictions_total: increased 4.2x since 09:58
p95_generate_latency: 720ms at peak, baseline 120ms
p99_generate_latency: 1.8s at peak
```

maria_sre: that looks like cache thrash. Could the key normalization change make keys higher-cardinality?

aj_runtime: yes. The v2.14.1 change tried to fix an earlier bug by adding session context to the prefix key: we accidentally included session_id when building prefix keys for KV. For most flows that was fine, but session_id has high entropy so it massively increased cardinality.

li_runtime: confirming — found code snippet before deploy: 
```
// old (pre-change)
String key = prefix + ":" + model + ":" + user_id;
// v2.14.1 introduced
String key = prefix + ":" + model + ":session:" + session_id + ":" + user_id;
```
Session_id gets regenerated frequently -> cache never reuses entries, causing high eviction and cold misses.

maria_sre: ouch. any quick mitigation we can do while we prepare a rollback/patch?

aj_runtime: immediate options: 1) rollback deploy 2) hotfix server-side normalization to strip session_id from cache key 3) bump cache size temporarily 4) pin hot prefixes (hot key table) 5) add singleflight to coalesce in-flight identical requests (reduces stampede).

tim_oncall: rollback looks safest short-term. What is impact of rollback on other fixes in that deploy?

aj_runtime: the batching kernel tweak is low-risk but acceptable to roll back together. We can rollback deploy-2026-03-15-0958 to restore previous behavior. Rollback path is tested.

maria_sre: do it. Tim, can you trigger rollback and monitor? Devon, tell customers we're escalating and a rollback is in progress.

ops-bot: Rolling back deploy-2026-03-15-0958...

tim_oncall: rollback initiated at 10:20 UTC. will post status.

aj_runtime: simultaneously creating hotfix branch to remove session_id from keygen and add a unit test to prevent future regressions. Also will add a normalization util: cache_key_for(prefix, model, user_id) -> stable deterministic.

devon_support: notified customers of rollback start. They'll hold for follow-up. Cases 8421/8423 updated.

li_runtime: monitoring after rollback — initial numbers look promising: kv_cache_miss_rate trending down. promoting additional metrics: cache_key_cardinality_by_prefix shows previously 15k unique keys for prefix X now back to ~2.2k.

maria_sre: paste p95/p99 after rollback (10:28 -> 10:32 window)?

li_runtime: p95 dropped from 720ms -> 140ms, p99 -> 220ms in 10:32 snapshot.

devon_support: customers reporting improved latency in first replies. One customer saw their app p99 go from 1.9s to ~230ms.

aj_runtime: good. still want to push hotfix to avoid reintroducing in future and to add protections. Proposed changes in hotfix:
- remove session_id from key composition
- replace LRU eviction with LFU for KV layer to resist single-session churn
- add singleflight (request coalescing) around cache misses for the next 30s window
- add metric kv_cache_key_components{prefix,has_session_id} so we can alert on session_id leakage
- add unit+integration tests to assert key cardinality under synthetic sessions

olga_product: can we also add a support doc or KB to explain warmup & what customers see? QA might want a postmortem blurb.

maria_sre: yes file a short blurb, but prioritize code fix + tests + automated guardrails.

aj_runtime: timeline: patch & tests by EOD today, small canary to 5% then ramp. Meanwhile keep LFU flagged as feature-flag off by default; canary will enable.

tim_oncall: monitoring playbook for next 24h: check kv_cache_miss_rate, kv_eviction_rate, p95/p99 per region, and alert if miss_rate > 30% or p99 > 1s.

devon_support: updating cases and internal notes. Assigning follow-up ticket INF-1724 to track patch + KB.

li_runtime: one additional note — the cache key bug only affected prefix-mode caching (per-prefix KV namespace), not global embedding cache. Confirmed via segment metrics.

maria_sre: thanks team. Postmortem actions: 1) revert risky key changes without canary 2) add automated cardinality check during CI that runs simple generator that simulates session ids and ensures cardinality stays below threshold 3) create alert for sudden spike in key-cardinality 4) add canary window for key-gen changes

aj_runtime: will create PR with tests and add key-cardinality Prometheus exporter. PR link when ready.

ops-bot: Rollback completed at 10:29:12 UTC :white_check_mark:

tim_oncall: verified nodes stabilized. Marking incident mitigated, but leaving monitoring on.

devon_support: customers acknowledged the rollback; keeping open until patch deployed. Thanks. :thumbsup:

maria_sre: assigning owners: aj_runtime -> hotfix PR + LFU experiment, li_runtime -> dashboards & alert, devon_support -> customer comms, tim_oncall -> monitoring runbook. Will schedule a 1-hour follow-up at 16:00 UTC to review the hotfix canary.

aj_runtime: quick snippet of suggested normalized key implementation:
```
String normalize(String s) { return s.replaceAll("\\s+"," ").toLowerCase(); }
String cacheKey(String prefix, String model, String user) {
  return prefix + ":" + model + ":" + sha256(normalize(user));
}
```
Note: hashing user_id reduces key length and avoids leaking session tokens.

li_runtime: logging a synthetic test to CI: generate 50k requests with random session_ids but same prefix/user -> ensure produced unique cache keys <= 5k.

maria_sre: good. add a regression test that fails the PR if cardinality exceeds threshold.

devon_support: adding KB stub: "Why you're seeing latency spikes after a deploy" — will include guidance on warmup, cache thrash, and how we handle rollbacks.

olga_product: perfect. include an explanation of 'hot key pinning' and when we'd use it.

maria_sre: closing notes: incident labeled INC-2026-0315-KV-THRASH. postmortem draft assigned to aj_runtime. If anyone has extra findings, drop them here.

aj_runtime: PR opened: https://git.company.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4520 (hotfix remove-session-id + tests) — canary planned 15:00 UTC.

tim_oncall: will monitor canary and run through runbook. thanks everyone.

devon_support: closing thread for now, will reopen if customers see regression.

maria_sre: :eyes: great job — nice quick detection and rollback.
